equation_request.abstract: We introduce a simple diagrammatic approach for estimating how a randomly walking quantum particle searches on a graph in continuous-time, which involves sketching small weighted graphs with self-loops and considering degenerate perturbation theory’s effects on them. Using this method, we give the first example of degenerate perturbation theory solving search on a graph whose evolution occurs in a subspace whose dimension grows with $N$.

specification.problem: Estimate how a continuous-time quantum walk searches on a graph by sketching small weighted graphs with self-loops and applying degenerate perturbation theory, including a case where evolution occurs in a subspace whose dimension grows with N.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of the search model only: continuous-time quantum walk search with a marked-vertex oracle Hamiltonian and degenerate perturbation theory on effective small weighted graphs. Specific graphs, results and circuits are not given in the abstract.

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard continuous-time quantum walk search Hamiltonian with graph Laplacian L, hopping rate gamma and marked vertex w; assumed form, not stated in the abstract.
equations.justification: Common CTQW search model; the abstract mentions a randomly walking particle searching a graph but gives no formula.
assumptions: Marked vertex w; Laplacian-type hopping term

equations.label: Degenerate perturbation theory
equations.latex: H_{\mathrm{eff}} = P V P + \sum_{k\notin D} \frac{P V |k\rangle\langle k| V P}{E_0-E_k}
equations.description: Effective Hamiltonian on degenerate subspace D of H_0 with projector P, up to second order.
equations.justification: Standard degenerate perturbation theory background, which the abstract says is used.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Position of the walker on the graph vertices; the walk is simulated as Hamiltonian evolution, not a gate-based circuit

specification.initial_state: Assumed uniform superposition over all vertices, (1/sqrt(N)) sum_v |v>, the usual CTQW search start; not stated in the abstract.

steps.description: Prepare the assumed uniform superposition on the vertex register.
Evolve under the search Hamiltonian H for a time t, which is assumed to be implemented via Hamiltonian simulation.
Analyze the dynamics by restricting to the degenerate subspace and using the effective Hamiltonian, which corresponds to a small weighted graph with self-loops.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after evolution for time t, measure the vertex register in the computational (vertex) basis and read out the marked vertex w with probability |<w|psi(t)>|^2. Not specified in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: repeat the evolve-and-measure procedure, check whether the outcome is the marked vertex using the oracle, and repeat if not. The evolution time is chosen near the peak success probability from the effective small-graph analysis. Not specified in the abstract.
